evals.prompt: I need a 20-slide deck for our Q3 business review next week. Can you write it?
evals.expected_output: Do not jump straight to slide copy. Start at stage 1 (blueprint): ask for or derive the ONE message as a falsifiable claim (not 'Q3 review'), the audience and what they care about, 2-3 emotional angles, and only then challenge the 20-slide count ('20 slides for one meeting usually means three decks'). Proceed through the stages in order — blueprint, structure, story frame, visual direction, content, build — each in its own prompt with the previous artifact as input, and state the gate that must pass before the next stage.
expectations: Refuses to produce slide copy immediately and starts with the blueprint stage
Requires the single message to be a claim, not a topic
Questions or justifies the slide count instead of accepting it
Keeps the stages in order with the previous artifact as input
Names a gate/check before advancing

evals.prompt: My sales deck has 14 slides and every one is a title plus six bullet points of 20 words. It reads like a document. What do I change?
evals.expected_output: Diagnose it as bullet walls, not a formatting issue: the deck skipped the blueprint/structure stages, so each slide has no purpose line and the copy is carrying the argument. Fix in order: (1) write the one-sentence message and each slide's one-line purpose, deleting slides without a distinct job; (2) map the remainder onto Hook/Problem/Insight/Solution/Proof/Takeaway with a single ask at the end; (3) rewrite titles to <=6 words and bullets to 3-5 of <=10 words, moving the prose into speaker notes so the argument is spoken, not displayed; (4) run deck_lint.py to enforce the limits mechanically and render the slides to check overflow.
expectations: Diagnoses missing blueprint/structure rather than treating it as a styling problem
Requires one-line purpose per slide and deletion of slides without a distinct job
Applies the story frame with exactly one action on the final slide
Enforces <=6-word titles and 3-5 bullets of <=10 words, moving prose into notes
Recommends deck_lint.py plus a rendered visual check

evals.prompt: Which chart should I use for our revenue by region over 8 quarters, and how do I phrase the slide title?
evals.expected_output: Stage 4 answer: bar for the regional comparison (or line for trend within each region if the change over time is the point), one chart per idea, one number called out. Stage 5 answer for the title: a <=6-word claim, not a label — e.g. 'EMEA grew, APAC stalled' rather than 'Revenue by region Q1-Q8' — with the takeaway in the speaker note and at most a three-colour palette. Note the deck-level constraint: the plot must support the deck's single message.
expectations: Chooses the chart from the communicative job (comparison vs trend) and justifies it
Rejects label-style titles in favour of a <=6-word claim
Keeps to one chart/one idea/one number
Ties the choice back to the deck's single message

evals.prompt: Can you check this deck.pptx for me — titles too long, too many bullets, missing speaker notes?
evals.expected_output: Run the bundled linter rather than eyeballing it: `uv run --with python-pptx scripts/deck_lint.py deck.pptx` (or with tuned --max-title-words/--max-bullets flags), report its JSON findings per slide, and follow up on what the linter cannot see — render the slides and check overflow, contrast and orphaned bullets. Do not claim the deck is fine without running something.
expectations: Uses the deck_lint.py script instead of manual counting
Reports concrete per-slide findings with the rule that fired
Adds the visual/render check the linter cannot perform
Does not assert quality without an actual run

evals.prompt: Give me the visual direction for a 6-slide investor pitch about a grid-scale battery startup.
evals.expected_output: Stay in stage 4 and output per-slide: the emotion the visual carries, the chart or single big number for the data, icon/grid treatment for lists, one three-colour palette with hex codes, and one heading/body font pairing available in standard Office/Google fonts. Describe composition, not stock-photo subjects, and keep the palette/fonts constant across all six slides.
expectations: Produces per-slide emotional intent plus chart-choice reasoning
Supplies one three-colour palette with hex codes and one font pairing
Describes composition instead of naming stock photos
Keeps the visual system constant across slides

evals.prompt: Convert this deck.pptx to PDF and rename the file for me.
evals.expected_output: Out of scope for this skill — it is a format/mechanical operation (soffice/LibreOffice conversion), not deck planning or review. Point at the format-conversion route and do not run the six-stage pipeline.
expectations: Recognises the request as format conversion, outside the pipeline
Does not invoke the blueprint/structure/content stages
Points at the mechanical conversion route instead

evals.prompt: Write me a 40-slide internal wiki page about our onboarding process.
evals.expected_output: Not a presentation task: the artifact requested is a reference document, where length and completeness are assets. Say so and suggest a document format rather than applying slide constraints (six-word titles, five bullets) that would destroy the reference value. If a slide version is genuinely wanted later, the pipeline applies to a summary deck derived from the document.
expectations: Identifies the artifact as a document, not a deck
Declines to impose slide constraints on reference material
Offers the pipeline only for a derived summary deck
